issues.where: ch09-s07 L0920 'Give RegExp eight workers, and the GPU isn't clearly faster.'
issues.problem: This understates the other side of contested JS13. The bible's settled view (sec. 3 E6, line 309) is 'not faster than 8 workers except on the backtracking pattern'. After a pause, which is what a human typing actually gets (JS19), the GPU takes 2-8x as long as RegExp in 8 workers. 'Isn't clearly faster' still leans toward the GPU.
issues.fix: Say: 'Give RegExp eight workers, and it wins, except on the one pattern that makes it backtrack.' Extend the 'workers' label: 'RegExp in 8 workers: 1.9–6.7 ms · GPU: 4.5–5.2 ms back to back, 2–8× as long after a pause'. Add JS19 to claims if the pause is mentioned.

issues.where: ch09-s05 L0911 'First backwards, noting where a match could still finish; then forwards, counting.' (and the visual's per-state notes and the 'tally')
issues.problem: JS06 and the dossier (demo-json-search.md L217-L224) support only this: two passes, reverse then forward, 'since a longest match is only known after reading past its end, and a program can't go back'. Neither describes what the reverse pass records or says the forward pass counts. The shot's notes 'could a match still finish from here?' and its tally are an unverified mechanism presented as fact.
issues.fix: Ground it in the repo's own reason: 'First from the end, then from the start: a longest match is only known after reading past its end.' Drop 'counting' and the per-state note semantics from the visual, or verify them in src/json-search/search-step.ts and add a claim before keeping them.

strengths: 17 of the round-1 accuracy items were fixed precisely and in the source's own terms: the 'not attributable to Cheng' card, 'Eighty-three years on' with the in-between makers shown, '15 to 27 times slower' (crossing Bun and Chrome honestly), 'almost every whole number', 'that one among them', the undated 0/20, the LB26 open questions voiced, and the 'regular JavaScript' tagline acknowledged at the end.

Quote integrity is otherwise excellent. All 45 quoted spans in narration and on screen are verbatim from quotes.json, attributed at the right level ('the docs', 'the HandwiredOS README', 'Cheng Lou · in the lab's gallery notes', 'a Hacker News commenter'), and quoted only where the repo marks Cheng's words. Cheng's informal register ('Do it quick plz, then publish.') is kept as written.

Every worked number checks under FP32: the 4.5 -> 11 and 4.25 -> 11.5 dimmer, 16,777,222 -> 8, the tie-to-even 0.5 -> 8,388,610 -> 1, the 1732 px column count, the two row sums one FP32 step apart, the spring step, the valve gradients, the Adam step to about 0.492 (marked 'derived').

Honest scoping is consistent: 'in its tests' for bit-identity, 'float64 copy' for the 359 px drift, 'one machine · Chrome 155 · RegExp on one thread' on the timings, 'an older 14,019-operation build' on the GPU figure, 'a prefix network only in a later reading' for Sklansky, and 'an echo, not a citation' for Kleene in ch09.

The AI-tooling passage (ch08-s07) follows the bible's even-handedness guidance to the letter. Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex are named in the same factual register, 'This film was written with Claude' is said once and plainly, and the mistakes and catches are framed as one process under Cheng's direction rather than as a vendor scorecard.

The contested matters now give both sides: Sutton and Brooks, snap vs carry framed as a design choice, 'fully differentiable' doubted by the repo itself, JSON recovery including the agent-written row where the rules win, the TOML failure with the README's own caveat, and 'The record doesn't say why. So we won't guess.' for August.
